clue.text: Account by about 21 people in court?

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
the solution to 21 across, meaning pre-owned

explanation.surface: Someone gives a statement while referring to the defendants standing in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the answer of 21 across, which is added after AC and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Those on trial in a courtroom are collectively called the defendants, hence the question mark for this loose sense.

clue.text: Inspire article about what follows funeral

indicators.note: about means around, so the article is wrapped round the next piece

parts.note: AN is the indefinite article
a wake is the gathering held after a funeral

explanation.surface: An oddly specific instruction to motivate a newspaper piece on post-funeral events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece but is the grammatical article; a wake is the gathering after a burial.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse or stir up a feeling in someone is to inspire it, as in awaken interest.

clue.text: Spiritual leader lacking energy in chapel I roused

indicators.note: roused means stirred up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lacking means going without, so the letter for energy is dropped

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A clergyman without vigour is stirred into action inside his chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking energy' removes E from CHAPEL, leaving CHAPL; with I, 'roused' rearranges CHAPLI.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic head of the Islamic world held both religious and civil authority, so spiritual leader fits.

clue.text: Paper is after loan before editor's removed

indicators.note: is after puts the word for paper following the word for loan
before places the preceding pieces ahead of the abbreviation for editor

parts.note: a sub is an advance or loan on wages
a tract is a short paper or pamphlet

explanation.surface: A newspaper chases a loan before its editor is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of editor's is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken away, as a number from a total, means the same as taken off.

clue.text: Go right inside disreputable bar

indicators.note: inside says the letter for right sits within the word for a bar

parts.note: a dive is a seedy, disreputable bar

explanation.surface: Head straight into a seedy pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel by car or motor along is to go, as in we'll go there by road.

clue.text: Recover from fresh miracle

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of the following word made new, reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A sufferer gets better thanks to a new miracle cure.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something back that was lost is to take it back again, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Thought to take out large meal

indicators.note: to take out says the letter for large is removed

parts.note: reflection is careful thought
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone considers ordering a big takeaway dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take out' looks like takeaway food but means remove; L comes out of REFLECTION. The answer is an old word for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word for refreshment by food is a light repast, hence the refectory where monks ate.

clue.text: Cleaner reluctant to scrub yard

indicators.note: to scrub means to cancel or delete, so the letter for yard goes

parts.note: chary means wary or reluctant

explanation.surface: A cleaner who does not want to scrub the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrub' looks like cleaning work but means delete. A char is a British word for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman, shortened, is a person paid to clean houses or offices.

clue.text: Before noon, one Liberal Democrat's friendly

parts.note: AM means ante meridiem, before noon
I is the Roman numeral for one
Vince Cable was a leader of the UK Liberal Democrat party

explanation.surface: A politician from a centrist party is cheerful in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable led Britain's Liberal Democrats from 2017 to 2019; the 's stands for is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on good terms and getting along well is the meaning of both words, a synonym.

clue.text: Imagination Disney stirred up inside me

indicators.note: inside places the rearranged letters within the following word
stirred up means mixed, so the letters of the film company's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fantasy films from Disney stir something within the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside me' reads as emotion but is a container instruction: the shuffled film-studio name sits between M and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The inward faculty of picturing things in thought is the mind's capacity for visualising, i.e. fancy.

clue.text: Spontaneous remark from District Attorney upset lawyers in Boston, initially

indicators.note: in a down clue sense, upset means knocked over, so the letters are turned back to front

parts.note: DA is the usual abbreviation for a US District Attorney

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the words lawyers, in and Boston

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor makes an offhand comment about Boston's legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DA round; 'initially' takes the first letters of lawyers, in, Boston.
explanation.definitionFit: An improvised line spoken without preparation is the usual meaning of this theatrical term.

clue.text: Cause of increase in damage?

parts.note: damage here is slang for cost (what's the damage?), and rising prices are what pushes the cost of things up

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what made some harm worse, perhaps an insurance question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' is informal for the price of something; the answer is the economic force raising prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A general rise in prices across an economy is precisely what increases the bill you pay.

clue.text: Specialist almost spoilt niece's encounter

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: an expert is a specialist

indicators.note: spoilt suggests the following word damaged and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A professional nearly ruins a young relative's meeting with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims EXPERT to EXPER; 'spoilt' rearranges NIECE into IENCE; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo or meet with something is a verb sense matching encounter, as in to come across difficulties.

clue.text: Fish deep

definitions.meaning: a low-pitched voice or sound, the lowest singing range

explanation.surface: Just two words: a fish living far below the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves both the fish and the musical term for low pitch, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Unsettled at home and fed up, I fool with ecstasy

parts.note: IN means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A person feeling restless at home, fed up and keeping company with a party drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' looks like an idiom for annoyed but means FED reversed, giving DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Not yet fixed or decided, without a set limit, is what unsettled means here.

clue.text: Provoke colleague from time to time

parts.note: to occasion something is to cause or provoke it
an ally is a partner or colleague

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a workmate now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and then, at irregular intervals, is the adverb's exact meaning.

clue.text: A goddess intended to be heartless for fun

parts.note: the Muses were the nine Greek goddesses of the arts

indicators.note: heartless asks for the middle letter of the word for intended to be removed

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A goddess planned to be cruel just for the sport of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central A from MEANT, leaving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment and enjoyment are what both words describe, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Oscar caught by copper and possibly spotted getting tied up

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
CU is the chemical symbol for copper
pied means of two or more colours, patched, so possibly spotted

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winner is arrested by a policeman, perhaps noticed while being bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy or engaged with something, unable to do anything else, is the meaning shared.

clue.text: Nuts aren't about to worry animal

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the word for worry
nuts means crazy, so the letters of aren't are thrown into a new order

parts.note: to eat someone is to worry or trouble them, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: Crazy people deny they are about to fret over a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' rearranges ARENT into ANTER, which goes 'about' EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-snouted mammal feeding on insects is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Results obtained from prisoner with chains

parts.note: CON is short for convict, a prisoner
chains of events are sequences, things following one after another

explanation.surface: The outcome of keeping an inmate shackled.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcomes that follow from an action are its effects, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Toy instrument

definitions.meaning: to toy with something is to ..., fidget with it
the violin is informally called this

explanation.surface: Just two words: a plaything that makes music.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as the verb to fidget idly and as the informal name of the violin.

clue.text: Burbank — a rather gripping city

indicators.note: gripping says the words hold the answer within them, spanning their breaks

explanation.surface: The Californian town of Burbank is rather an exciting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' looks like exciting but means holding.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Turkey, an example of a city.

clue.text: Bond ignoring female with diamonds, pre-owned

indicators.note: ignoring says to leave out the letter that stands for female

parts.note: to fuse things is to bond them together
D is the card-game abbreviation for the diamonds suit

explanation.surface: James Bond, uninterested in women, sells second-hand jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like 007 but means fuse; 'ignoring female' removes F to leave USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have had an earlier owner, so they are not new.

clue.text: Appeal again for rehearsal

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
a petition is a formal appeal or request

explanation.surface: Asking once more to be allowed to practise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-PETITION, a petition made again.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over something again and again is how rehearsal works, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Plane on time for get-together

parts.note: a plane surface is level or even

explanation.surface: An aircraft arrives punctually for a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks like an aircraft but means flat.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised occasion where people gather is a meeting or function.

clue.text: Melody from American lifted atmosphere

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means raised, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: air is atmosphere

explanation.surface: A tune from the US is carried up through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns AIR upwards into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo song is a tune, so melody fits loosely.

clue.text: Put out fire — enter block

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or disordered, so the letters of fire and enter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firefighter's instruction: extinguish the flames and go into the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like extinguish; it is the anagram signal for FIRE plus ENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle or obstruct is to hinder something, so block works as a verb synonym.

clue.text: Financial help rejected by one northern country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: aid is financial assistance

explanation.surface: A northern nation turns down monetary assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected by' places the reversed word after the letters for one and northern.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large South Asian nation, the definition being simply its category.

clue.text: Do shout to limit male's sleeping

indicators.note: to limit means to enclose, so the word for shout holds the letter for male inside it

parts.note: to rant is to shout angrily

explanation.surface: An order to yell in order to restrain a man who is asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to limit' puts M inside RANT after its first letter, giving RMANT; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive or asleep, as a volcano or a seed lying quiet, is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Some get here safely in May?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looks like a wish that travellers arrive safely during the month of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' is not the month but the surname of the former UK Prime Minister; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019 had this first name, completed by the surname May.
